paragraphs: Hi, I'm Matt Atrard. I own Faber Roof in Farmington Hills. I am chasing commercial roofs: flat roofs, TPO roofs, large complexes, and property managers who have a lot of buildings and have put the work off. You call. Someone looks at the roof. You get the bid in writing.

We can put up to 20 workers on a roof and do thousands of squares a week. A lot of crews are 4 or 5 people, and they cannot turn that kind of job. We are a Mulehide-certified installer. Mulehide is the Firestone membrane brand. On most roofs we service, the warranty is 10 years on labor and material. We do not cut corners. We do it the right way every time.

Residential is still here. It is not the campaign. A homeowner said the cleanup looked like the crew was never there. A commercial customer said the job finished on budget and on time. Call (810) 360-7385 and say which one you are.

decision.label: Repair or replace
decision.title: Repair or replace?
decision.intro: A stain on the ceiling means water already beat the shingles. You should not have to chase roofers who never call back or approve a price with no scope. We get on the roof and tell you repair or replacement — in writing.

repair.title: A repair usually makes sense when
items: The leak is in one spot, like a pipe boot, a chimney, or a skylight
Wind took off a handful of shingles and the rest still lie flat
Flashing has pulled loose and the deck under it still feels solid

replace.title: Replacement usually makes sense when
items: Shingles are curling, cracking, or shedding granules into the gutters
Leaks keep showing up in new places
There are already two layers of shingles

decision.note: If you only want the cheapest handyman patch on failing shingles, we are probably not your crew. Patches on worn roofs often cost twice when the next storm hits. A winter stain along an outside wall can also be an ice dam — we look at the eave before we tell you the whole roof is done.

faqs.q: Should I repair my roof or replace it?
faqs.a: If the problem is in one spot and the rest of the roof still lies flat, a repair usually makes sense. If shingles are curling or shedding granules, leaks keep moving, or the deck feels soft, replacement is usually the better spend. We say which one we would choose after we look. Call (810) 360-7385.

faqs.q: How do I get an estimate?
faqs.a: Call (810) 360-7385 or send the form. Someone looks at the roof, then you get the scope and the price in writing.

faqs.q: How long does a roof replacement take?
faqs.a: One homeowner said their tear-off and new shingles were done in a day. Steeper roofs, attached homes, and commercial jobs take longer. The estimate includes the schedule.

faqs.q: Do you work on attached homes and commercial buildings?
faqs.a: Yes. Houses, attached homes, and commercial roofs. A commercial customer said their job finished on budget and on time. Property managers get the same thing homeowners get: a look, then a written estimate.

faqs.q: Do you install TPO and flat roofs?
faqs.a: Yes. Commercial flat roofing and TPO roofs are the main service, for property managers and commercial owners. Call (810) 360-7385 and ask for a bid.

faqs.q: How large a crew can you put on a roof?
faqs.a: Up to 20 workers, and thousands of squares a week. A lot of crews in this market are 4 or 5 people. That is the difference on a complex or a 40- to 50-building list.
A 10-year labor and material warranty on most roofs we service. We are a Mulehide-certified installer. Mulehide is the Firestone membrane brand.
Yes. Residential is separate from commercial, and it is not the lead offer. Use the residential inquiry, or call (810) 360-7385 and say it is a house.
Yes. 0% financing options with 12 to 24 month terms, subject to credit approval. Ask when you get the estimate.
Storm leaks get priority when we can reach them. Call (810) 360-7385 and we will tell you the next opening.

faqs.q: Will you roof over the old shingles?
faqs.a: Usually no. A second layer hides a soft deck and fails sooner. If there are already two layers, those come off. We say what we find after someone is on the roof.

faqs.q: What if the deck is soft?
faqs.a: Soft plywood gets replaced before new shingles go down. The estimate names the bad spots we can see. If more shows up after tear-off, you hear about it before anyone covers it.
Most Metro Detroit cities want a permit for a replacement. When your city requires one, that paperwork is part of the job. Call (810) 360-7385 and we will tell you what your address needs.

faqs.q: Can you work with my insurance after a storm?
faqs.a: We can look at storm damage and write what the roof needs. You still deal with your insurer. The estimate is based on the roof, not on a guess from the adjuster’s photo.

faqs.q: What if it rains on the day of the job?
faqs.a: Tear-off does not start if the deck would sit open in a storm. If weather turns during the day, the open slope gets covered before the crew leaves.
Farmington Hills, Detroit, and nearby towns including Farmington, Novi, Livonia, Northville, Southfield, and Plymouth. Call (810) 360-7385 to confirm your address.
